It’s like my mind is racing; I’m starting projects I never finish, and even though I’ve only slept a few hours, I wake up wired and ready to go. I’ve been spending money like crazy too, on things we don’t need. While I’m up in the crane, it’s not the heights that bother me, it’s the thought that everything is just… crumbling. I keep having these visions of structures failing, of the ground opening up. It feels so real, like the end is nigh and people just aren't seeing it. Other times, I feel invincible, able to accomplish anything, and these worries about the world just vanish. Then the dread creeps back, and I find myself watching the news, convinced every report is a sign of the impending collapse. It’s making it hard to focus, both at home and at work.
D004-D010_h001.question_a:
It's been... well, it feels like forever, but I'd say at least nine months now. I've been seeing signs everywhere, on the news, even on the job – the way the crane sways sometimes – that the world is on the brink. Not just a bad spell, but like, everything is going to collapse. I see it in how my wife looks at me, how the guys at work are so oblivious. I try to warn them, but they just laugh.

I've had my ups and downs, sure. A few weeks here and there, I'd get this burst of energy, barely sleep, feel like I could accomplish anything. I'd be chatting up a storm, planning all sorts of things with my wife. But that always fades. The feeling that everything is crumbling, that's constant. It's there whether I'm buzzing with energy or just feeling normal. I'm still able to go to work, operate the crane, and my wife says I'm mostly myself, just... fixated. But this dread, it never goes away.
D004-D010_h001.question_b: "It's like the world’s coming to an end, doctor. Everything feels… hollow. I keep seeing these cracks, not just in the walls, but in the sky, like it's all about to shatter. Usually, I'm pretty steady, focused on my crane work, but lately, it's been hard to concentrate. There are days, weeks even, where I'm buzzing with energy, barely sleeping, just going and going, feeling like I can achieve anything – that's when these visions and thoughts really kick in, when the feeling of impending doom is overwhelming, but also strangely exhilarating. My wife says I'm not myself; I bought a new boat last month without even talking to her, I just *had* to have it, to outrun what's coming. I know it sounds crazy, but I truly believe the world is disintegrating, and it’s especially terrifying when I’m feeling this high. Then, things crash, and I just want to stay in bed, numb to it all again. But then the cycle repeats, and that feeling of the world breaking apart returns, always alongside that burst of energy and sleepless nights."
